why_critical: Pay once per record/requester pair while preserving independent requester eligibility.
Prevent ordinary wallets from selecting an issuer or minting their own points.
Reject unverified record publication without consuming an id.
Store the patient's identity commitment and role without granting verification automatically.
Prevent a second signup from overwriting the original identity.
Require verification again after identity details change.
Associate the blood-panel commitment and type with its correct patient.
Prevent patients from approving their own verification.
Only a reviewed identity should become eligible for verified-patient operations.
Stop access at expiry or withdrawal and prevent repeated renewal rewards.
Give only the chosen doctor scoped, time-limited access while retaining patient ownership.
Keep the patient's disclosure decisions under the patient's control.
Enforce the assignment's 1-365-day consent duration boundaries.
Retain allowed and denied decisions without charging/moving reward points.
Make any stored-byte change affect the record commitment.
Keep the provided identity/record fixtures synthetic and consistently structured.
Make identity commitments independent of JSON key ordering.
Use a repeatable identity serialization and SHA-256 commitment.
Prevent two differently salted identity fixtures from sharing a commitment.
Establish real authorized delivery, decryption and persistent consumption.
Reject another wallet's signature without consuming the doctor's authorization.
